spec.name: int-sdiv-smod-minus-one-widths-p0-int8-provenance

panel.evidence: Source: a = type(int8).min (-128), b = -1; call divStored performs a / b. EVM reverts (dry-run and committed status 'revert'), consistent with Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic where INT_MIN / -1 = 128 overflows int8 and panics (Panic 0x11). Polkadot reports success; committed storage shows last = -128 and count = 1, i.e. solang silently wrapped the result to -128 (0x80) instead of reverting.
panel.rationale: In Solidity >=0.8, signed division of the minimum value by -1 is a checked operation that must revert with a panic, since the mathematical result (+128) is not representable in int8. The solang run returned success with last = -128, indicating missing overflow detection on signed division (or constant-folded signed division) in solang's Polkadot codegen. The divergence is deterministic, semantic, and not explained by environment values, gas, or oracle projection: the storage-count mode merely reflects that EVM state was rolled back while Polkadot state committed.
panel.cluster_hint: solang missing overflow revert for signed division INT_MIN / -1 (int8), wrapping instead of panicking

panel.evidence: EVM dry-run and committed tx revert for divStored() with a = type(int8).min (-128), b = -1; solang/Polkadot returns success and stores last=-128, count=1. Per Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic semantics, INT8_MIN / -1 overflows int8 range and must panic (revert), which solc does. Solang produced the wrapped result -128 without reverting.
panel.rationale: Solidity >=0.8.0 requires overflow-checked division, and -128 / -1 = +128 is not representable in int8, so the correct behavior is a reverting panic. The EVM oracle reverts as expected, while solang silently wraps to -128 and increments count. This is a semantic defect in solang's signed division codegen for narrow integer types, not an environment, oracle-projection, or gas artifact.
panel.cluster_hint: solang missing signed-division overflow check for narrow signed ints (int8 min / -1 wraps instead of panicking)

adversarial.evidence: The contract performs a/b with a = type(int8).min (-128) and b = -1 under pragma >=0.8.0. Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic mandates a revert (Panic 0x11) because +128 is unrepresentable in int8; the EVM oracle reverts in both dry-run and committed transaction. Solang/Polkadot instead returns success and commits last = -128 (0x80, the exact two's-complement wrap of +128) with count = 1. The stored value being precisely the wrapped result, rather than garbage or an environment-dependent value, indicates the division executed without an overflow check. The divergence involves none of the documented known-difference markers (no block/tx environment reads, gas comparison disabled, oracle storage projection only reflects the revert-vs-success split rather than causing it). None of the supplied historical records describe this behavior, so rediscovery cannot be established from the given evidence.
adversarial.rationale: This is a deterministic semantic divergence on a core language operation: solang fails to implement the Solidity 0.8 checked-arithmetic revert for signed division INT_MIN / -1 on int8, silently wrapping instead. It is not explained by platform environment values, gas models, or oracle artifacts, and no supplied historical record documents it as intended behavior or a known prior report. The evidence survives adversarial scrutiny.

history.title: Inconsistent behaviour when calling function via contract type name
Add Rename functionality
history.text:
This feature depends on having the right span information for identifiers in the parse tree. Currently, some changes are needed to either add the missing span information in some cases, or improve the already present spans (look for one-off errors). 

The rest of the "goto-*" functions also depend on the availability of proper spans. But in their case, as no modification is made to the source code, lack of accurate spans is less of an issue. But `rename` does modify the source code and hence having incorrect spans can result in unintentionally overwriting pieces of source code, which is highly undesirable. 

The changes made as part of this PR provide the necessary code for `rename` to work. Correcting the parse tree is expected to be done as part of future PRs

A non-exhaustive list of changes to be made to parse tree:  (https://github.com/hyperledger/solang/pull/1411#issuecomment-1648031602)

1. No loc for contract variables type - array_type_dynamic_push.sol L6
2. No loc for constructor base call - abstract_contract_inheritance.sol L14
3. No loc for function modifier arguments - function_modifier_arguments.sol L8
4. No loc for function override base contracts - virtua

history.title: Thread 'main' panicked  error when compiling call with seeds
thread 'main' panicked while compiling BlindAuction from Solidity official website
history.text:
**Describe the bug**
Solang failed to compile BlindAuction.sol, which is an example from the solidity [official website](https://github.com/raineorshine/solidity-by-example).

**To Reproduce**
The code I try to compile is [here](https://gist.github.com/yisun92/12e608b002cbc2b6db5b482fa11fa7e6)

I tried to compile the code using the following commands.
`solang compile --target solana -v BlindAuction.sol`
or
`solang compile --target substrate -v BlindAuction.sol
`
Both commands failed and threw the following error.
`thread 'main' panicked at 'Found PointerValue(PointerValue { ptr_value: Value { name: "elem", address: 0x600000f0c080, is_const: false, is_null: false, is_undef: false, llvm_value: "  %elem = bitcast i8* %index_access to i256*", llvm_type: "i256*" } }) but expected the IntValue variant', /Users/runner/.cargo/registry/src/github.com-1ecc6299db9ec823/inkwell-0.1.0-beta.4/src/values/enums.rs:269:13
`

If I remove the the code from line 73-82, the error is gone.

```solidity
if (bidToCheck.blindedBid != keccak256(abi.encodePacked(value, fake, secret))) {
    // Bid was not actually revealed.
    // Do not refund deposit.
    continue;
}
